## Overview {#sec-overview}

This project aims to characterize the variation in anti-adeno-associated virus (AAV) antibody eligibility criteria across AAV gene therapy clinical trials using the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database. By developing a hybrid Natural Language Processing (NLP) extraction pipeline, evaluating a local, open LLM architecture (utilizing \`Ollama\`/\`ellmer\`) against a \`tidyverse\` regex baseline, this study quantifies how key eligibility parameters (serotype, titer thresholds, and assay specifications) correlate with trial characteristics such as sponsor type, indication, and enrollment year. Project scope and clinical motivation were directly inspired by discussions with Dr. Lindsey George, MD (Pediatric Hematology, Penn/CHOP and PI on the Clinical In Vitro Gene Therapy (CIGT) group's biorepository/registry study), while technical foundations in AAV vector science and biological mechanisms were developed through trainings from Dr. Juliana Small, PhD (Regulatory Affairs and Clinical Development, CIGT at CHOP). All project code, documentation, and version control history are available in the \[BMIN5030 Final Project GitHub Repository\](https://github.com/naomi-k-lynch/BMIN5030_Final_Project).

## Introduction {#sec-introduction}

**Describe the problem addressed, its significance, and some background to motivate the problem. This should extend what is in the @sec-overview.**

Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors represent a leading platform for *in vivo* gene replacement therapy, offering transformative potential for genetic disorders such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), and hemophilia. However, pre-existing neutralizing or binding anti-AAV antibodies remain a primary obstacle to successful gene delivery, as host immune responses can compromise therapeutic efficacy and induce severe adverse reactions. Consequently, clinical trial protocols routinely establish strict serological exclusion criteria. Despite their clinical importance, these inclusion and exclusion metrics are highly unstandardized across trials, varying widely in titer thresholds, laboratory assay methodologies, and targeted vector serotypes. Analyzing these patterns across historical and active trials is critical for understanding access barriers to gene therapies and identifying broader trial design trends in precision medicine.

This issue is fundamentally interdisciplinary, requiring convergence across pediatric hematology/neurology, regulatory science, biomedical informatics, and computational linguistics. Clinical specialists provide the domain knowledge necessary to define meaningful serological parameters and interpret physiological endpoints, while regulatory specialists offer critical insight into trial protocol standards and compliance frameworks. Concurrently, data science and NLP methodologies enable the scalable parsing of unstructured clinical trial protocols stored within public repositories like AACT. This work is deeply rooted in real-world clinical operations: training from Dr. Juliana Small on the molecular science, mechanisms, and importance of AAV vectors provided the foundational biological framework for understanding these eligibility hurdles. Furthermore, insights from Dr. Lindsey George, serving as PI on the CIGT registry study, directly inspired the project's focus on clinical utility and real-world patient impact. Incorporating guidance from both leaders, this project bridges these domains by pairing rigorous cohort scoping - restricting analyses to interventional AAV trials - with transparent data extraction pipeline validation, evaluating local LLM parsing performance against deterministic regex baselines.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

Describe the data used and general methodological approach used to address the problem described in the @sec-introduction. Subsequently, incorporate full R code necessary to retrieve and clean data, and perform analysis. Be sure to include a description of code so that others (including your future self) can understand what you are doing and why.

### Methodological Approach & Data Source

To characterize how anti-adeno-associated virus (AAV) antibody eligibility criteria vary across gene therapy trials, this project utilizes a static snapshot from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database. AACT provides comprehensive, relational data covering all registered clinical studies.

Because AACT flat files are distributed as UTF-8 encoded, pipe-delimited (\`\|\`) text files corresponding to individual database tables, our analytical approach avoids memory bottlenecks by leveraging R (\`tidyverse\`). Rather than loading every table in full, we ingest only the required relational files (\`studies.txt\`, \`eligibilities.txt\`, \`brief_summaries.txt\`, etc), specify the pipe delimiter explicitly, and perform targeted filtering to isolate interventional AAV trials.

### Data Retrieval and Environment Setup

We'll begin by setting up our workspace and loading the necessary libraries for data manipulation, string parsing, and visualization.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Loading required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(lubridate)
library(patchwork)


# Setting path to local AACT flat files directory in my repo :)
# Update this path to match your local repository/data structure!
data_dir <- "flat_data_files" 
```

### Ingesting, Joining, and Filtering Core AACT Tables

To build our study cohort, we first want to load the various tables from AACT: studies (containing design characteristics, start years, and sponsors), elegibilities table (containing the unstructured inclusion/exclusion criteria text), interventions, keywords, summaries, and conditions. We join these datasets using the unique study identifier nct_id.

We also will take the time to filter out NCT ID's that are ANCA-associated vasculitis studies! They are caught in our regex matching because they share the same AAV acronym, but don't apply here.

```{r}
#| eval: false

# regex matching AAV, rAAV, scAAV, serotypes (AAV9, AAVrh74), and adeno-associated
aav_pattern <- "\\b(r|sc)?aav[0-9a-z]*\\b|adeno[- ]associated"

# --- STEP 1: Load core tables ---
studies_df       <- read_delim(file.path(data_dir, "studies.txt"), delim = "|", show_col_types = FALSE)
elig_df          <- read_delim(file.path(data_dir, "eligibilities.txt"), delim = "|", show_col_types = FALSE)
interventions_df <- read_delim(file.path(data_dir, "interventions.txt"), delim = "|", show_col_types = FALSE)
other_names_df   <- read_delim(file.path(data_dir, "intervention_other_names.txt"), delim = "|", show_col_types = FALSE)
keywords_df      <- read_delim(file.path(data_dir, "keywords.txt"), delim = "|", show_col_types = FALSE)
summaries_df     <- read_delim(file.path(data_dir, "brief_summaries.txt"), delim = "|", show_col_types = FALSE)
conditions_df    <- read_delim(file.path(data_dir, "conditions.txt"), delim = "|", show_col_types = FALSE)
sponsors_df <- read_delim(file.path(data_dir, "sponsors.txt"), delim = "|", show_col_types = FALSE)

# --- STEP 2: Union all matching NCT IDs across tables ---
ncts_studies <- studies_df %>%
  filter(
    grepl(aav_pattern, brief_title, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE) |
      grepl(aav_pattern, official_title, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pull(nct_id)

ncts_interventions <- interventions_df %>%
  filter(
    grepl(aav_pattern, name, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE) |
      grepl(aav_pattern, description, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pull(nct_id)

ncts_other_names <- other_names_df %>%
  filter(grepl(aav_pattern, name, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(nct_id)

ncts_keywords <- keywords_df %>%
  filter(grepl(aav_pattern, downcase_name, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(nct_id)

ncts_summaries <- summaries_df %>%
  filter(grepl(aav_pattern, description, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(nct_id)

# --- STEP 3: Identifying ANCA-associated vasculitis to remove false positives (getting caught in AAV) ---
vasculitis_ncts <- unique(c(
  studies_df %>%
    filter(
      grepl("anca[- ]associated|vasculitis", brief_title, ignore.case = TRUE) |
        grepl("anca[- ]associated|vasculitis", official_title, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    pull(nct_id),
  conditions_df %>%
    filter(grepl("anca[- ]associated|vasculitis", name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(nct_id),
  keywords_df %>%
    filter(grepl("anca[- ]associated|vasculitis", downcase_name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(nct_id)
))

# checking counts for all our IDs and filtered false positives!
clean_aav_ncts <- setdiff(all_aav_ncts, vasculitis_ncts)
cat("Excluded ANCA-vasculitis false positives:", length(intersect(all_aav_ncts, vasculitis_ncts)), "\n")
cat("Clean candidate AAV NCT IDs:", length(clean_aav_ncts), "\n")

```

As seen above, we now have 592 candidate NCT IDs, and we'fe filtered out 67 ANCA-vasculitis false positives. Now, let's make our master dataset that will contain all the AACT trials. First, we'll flatten all multi-row tables (interventions and conditions) to 1 row per NCT ID, and then we'll join everything!

```{r}
# --- STEP 4: Collapse multi-row tables to 1 row per NCT ID ---
interventions_collapsed <- interventions_df %>%
  filter(nct_id %in% all_aav_ncts) %>%
  group_by(nct_id) %>%
  summarise(
    intervention_names = paste(unique(na.omit(name)), collapse = "; "),
    intervention_descriptions = paste(unique(na.omit(description)), collapse = " | "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

conditions_collapsed <- conditions_df %>%
  filter(nct_id %in% all_aav_ncts) %>%
  group_by(nct_id) %>%
  summarise(
    conditions = paste(unique(na.omit(name)), collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sponsors_collapsed <- sponsors_df %>%
  filter(nct_id %in% clean_aav_ncts) %>%
  arrange(nct_id, desc(lead_or_collaborator == "lead")) %>%
  group_by(nct_id) %>%
  summarise(
    lead_sponsor = paste(unique(na.omit(name[lead_or_collaborator == "lead"])), collapse = "; "),
    lead_agency_class = paste(unique(na.omit(agency_class[lead_or_collaborator == "lead"])), collapse = "; "),
    all_sponsors = paste(unique(na.omit(name)), collapse = "; "),
    sponsor_agency_classes = paste(unique(na.omit(agency_class)), collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --- STEP 5: Build clean 1-row-per-trial master dataset ---
aav_master_df <- studies_df %>%
  filter(
    nct_id %in% clean_aav_ncts,
    grepl("interventional", study_type, ignore.case = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  select(
    nct_id, brief_title, official_title, phase, overall_status,
    enrollment, start_date, primary_completion_date, source, source_class
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    elig_df %>% select(nct_id, criteria, minimum_age, maximum_age, child, adult, older_adult),
    by = "nct_id"
  ) %>%
  left_join(interventions_collapsed, by = "nct_id") %>%
  left_join(conditions_collapsed, by = "nct_id") %>%
  left_join(sponsors_collapsed, by = "nct_id")

cat("Total unique interventional AAV trials captured:", nrow(aav_master_df), "\n")
```

```{r}
aav_master_df %>%
  filter(!(nct_id %in% ncts_studies)) %>%
  select(nct_id, brief_title, intervention_names, conditions) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  print(n = 15, width = Inf)
```

### Cohort Scoping and EDA

Following guidance from Dr. Lindsey George to ensure rigorous and focused cohort scoping, we restrict our dataset to interventional studies explicitly evaluating AAV vector gene therapies. We conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA) to verify sample size adequacy (N) across trial phases and enrollment years before text extraction.

```{r}
# 1. Overall cohort size and enrollment (N) summary across aav_master_df
cohort_overview <- aav_master_df %>%
  summarise(
    total_trials = n(),
    total_participants_n = sum(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_enrollment = median(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_enrollment = IQR(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_enrollment = min(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_enrollment = max(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_enrollment = sum(is.na(enrollment))
  )

print(cohort_overview)

# 2. Trial count and participant enrollment (N) across trial phases
phase_summary <- aav_master_df %>%
  mutate(phase = if_else(is.na(phase) | phase == "", "Not Specified / NA", phase)) %>%
  group_by(phase) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    pct_trials = round(n() / nrow(aav_master_df) * 100, 1),
    total_participants = sum(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_participants = median(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trials))

print(phase_summary)

# 3. Trial counts and enrollment by start/enrollment year
year_summary <- aav_master_df %>%
  mutate(start_year = year(as.Date(start_date))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(start_year)) %>%
  group_by(start_year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    total_participants = sum(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(start_year)

print(year_summary, n = Inf)

# 4. Lead sponsor agency class breakdown
sponsor_summary <- aav_master_df %>%
  mutate(
    lead_agency_class = if_else(
      is.na(lead_agency_class) | lead_agency_class == "",
      "Not Specified / NA",
      lead_agency_class
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(lead_agency_class) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    pct_trials = round(n() / nrow(aav_master_df) * 100, 1),
    total_participants = sum(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trials))

print(sponsor_summary)
```

Now that we've got the numbers, let's do some visualization! Here, I am going to create a chart that shows trial counts by phase on the left, and trial starts over time (by enrollment/start year) on the right.

```{r}

phase_plot_df <- aav_master_df %>%

# Panel B: Trial starts over time

  ) +

    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)

# Combine side by side
p_phase + p_year +

  )
```

### Regex-Based NLP Pipeline

To build our regex-based pipeline as a baseline before we benchmark an LLM pipeline, we start on section segmentation of critera text (inclusion vs exclusion). Below, we split the unstructured criteria text from our master dataframe to create separate fields so polarity (e.g. requiring seronegativity vs excluding seropositivity) can be evaluated properly.

```{r}
# Split unstructured criteria text into Inclusion and Exclusion blocks
aav_nlp_prep <- aav_master_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Normalize line breaks and whitespace artifacts
    criteria_clean = str_replace_all(criteria, "\\r\\n|\\r", "\n"),
    
    # Extract Inclusion block (everything before Exclusion Criteria header)
    inclusion_text = case_when(
      str_detect(criteria_clean, regex("exclusion criteria\\s*:?", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~
        str_extract(criteria_clean, regex("(?s).*?(?=exclusion criteria\\s*:?)", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      TRUE ~ criteria_clean
    ),
    
    # Extract Exclusion block (everything from Exclusion Criteria header onward)
    exclusion_text = if_else(
      str_detect(criteria_clean, regex("exclusion criteria\\s*:?", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      str_extract(criteria_clean, regex("(?s)exclusion criteria\\s*:?.*", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      NA_character_
    )
  )
```

Starting from aav_nlp_prep, we'll split on newlines, \~ delimiters, numbered items, and bullet markers to keep individual rules granular while filtering down to lines referencing antibodies, serostatus, or titers.

```{r}
# Broad recall dictionary for anti-AAV humoral immunity mentions
ab_mention_regex <- regex(
  paste0(
    "\\b(",
    "antibod(y|ies)|nab|nabs|tab|tabs|igg|igm|",
    "seropositiv(e|ity)|seronegativ(e|ity)|serostatus|serolog(y|ic|ical)|",
    "titer(s)?|titre(s)?|neutraliz(ing|ation)|neutralis(ing|ation)|",
    "binding antibod(y|ies)|pre[- ]?existing immunit(y|ies)|elisa|luminex",
    ")\\b"
  ),
  ignore_case = TRUE
)

# Expand to 1 row per criterion clause and isolate antibody-relevant lines
antibody_clauses_v2 <- aav_nlp_prep %>%
  select(nct_id, phase, lead_agency_class, start_date, enrollment, inclusion_text, exclusion_text) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(inclusion_text, exclusion_text),
    names_to = "section",
    values_to = "section_text"
  ) %>%
  mutate(section = str_remove(section, "_text")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(section_text)) %>%
  separate_rows(
    section_text,
    sep = "\\n+|~+|\\s+(?=[0-9]{1,2}\\.\\s)|\\s*[•\\*\\-]\\s+(?=[A-Z0-9])"
  ) %>%
  mutate(clause = str_squish(section_text)) %>%
  filter(nchar(clause) > 5) %>%
  filter(str_detect(clause, ab_mention_regex))
```

Broad antibody matching will pull in non-AAV clinical criteria, so the below code will drop clauses matching known non-AAV serology or inhibitor terms unless the clause also explicitly anchors to an AAV vector, capsid, or transgene.

```{r}
non_aav_ab_regex <- regex(
  "\\b(hiv|hepatitis\\s*[a-e]|hbv|hcv|hav|cmv|ebv|hsv|sars-cov-2|covid|factor\\s*(viii|ix|8|9)|fix|fviii|inhibitor|anti-drug)\\b",
  ignore_case = TRUE
)

vector_anchor_regex <- regex(
  "\\b((r|sc)?aav[- ]?(rh)?[0-9a-z]*|adeno[- ]associated|vector|capsid|transgene)\\b",
  ignore_case = TRUE
)

antibody_clauses_filtered <- antibody_clauses_v2 %>%
  mutate(
    has_vector_anchor = str_detect(clause, vector_anchor_regex),
    is_non_aav_noise  = str_detect(clause, non_aav_ab_regex)
  ) %>%
  filter(has_vector_anchor | !is_non_aav_noise)

```

Now that we have isolated to individual antibody-related clauses, deterministic regular expressions can extract our 4 core clinical eligibility parameters:

- **Target Serotype -** e.g. AAV9, AAVrh74, AAV5, AAV8, AAV2

- **Titer/Cutoff Threshold -** e.g. 1:5, 1:50, \< 1:10, \>= 1:100, or OD/units

- **Assay Methodology** - NAb neutralizing assay vs TAb total binding

- **Eligibility Rule Direction** - does the clause enforce a seronegative requirement or an exclusion cutoff?

```{r}
regex_baseline_clauses <- antibody_clauses_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    extracted_serotype = str_extract_all(
      clause,
      regex("\\b(r|sc)?aav[- ]?(rh)?[0-9]{1,2}[a-z0-9]*\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)
    ) %>% map_chr(~ paste(unique(toupper(.x)), collapse = "; ")),
    extracted_serotype = na_if(extracted_serotype, ""),
    
    extracted_titer = str_extract_all(
      clause,
      regex(
        "([<>≤≥]=?\\s*)?1\\s*:\\s*[0-9,]+|[<>≤≥]=?\\s*[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\\s*(u/ml|iu/ml|ng/ml|od)",
        ignore_case = TRUE
      )
    ) %>% map_chr(~ paste(unique(.x), collapse = "; ")),
    extracted_titer = na_if(extracted_titer, ""),
    
    extracted_assay = case_when(
      str_detect(clause, regex("neutraliz|neutralis|\\bnab(s)?\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)) &
        str_detect(clause, regex("binding|\\btab(s)?\\b|elisa|eclia|meso scale", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Both (NAb & TAb)",
      str_detect(clause, regex("neutraliz|neutralis|\\bnab(s)?\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Neutralizing Antibody (NAb)",
      str_detect(clause, regex("binding|\\btab(s)?\\b|elisa|eclia|meso scale|igg", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Total Binding Antibody (TAb)",
      TRUE ~ "Unspecified Serology"
    ),
    
    has_numeric_cutoff = !is.na(extracted_titer)
  )

# Clause-level summary counts
regex_baseline_clauses %>%
  summarise(
    total_clauses = n(),
    unique_trials = n_distinct(nct_id),
    clauses_with_serotype = sum(!is.na(extracted_serotype)),
    clauses_with_titer = sum(!is.na(extracted_titer))
  )

# Breakdown by assay type across filtered clauses
regex_baseline_clauses %>%
  count(extracted_assay, sort = TRUE)
```

Now, because a single trial may contain multiple antibody clauses across inclusion and exclusion criteria, we will roll the extracted clauses back up to the nct_id level and merge them onto aav_master_df so each trial in our cohort is labeled as having or lacking anti-AAV antibody restrictions.

```{r}
trial_ab_summary <- regex_baseline_clauses %>%
  group_by(nct_id) %>%
  summarise(
    has_ab_criteria = TRUE,
    ab_sections = paste(unique(section), collapse = "; "),
    serotypes_mentioned = paste(unique(na.omit(extracted_serotype)), collapse = "; "),
    titer_cutoffs = paste(unique(na.omit(extracted_titer)), collapse = "; "),
    assay_types = paste(unique(extracted_assay), collapse = "; "),
    has_numeric_cutoff = any(has_numeric_cutoff),
    matched_clauses = paste(clause, collapse = " || "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    serotypes_mentioned = na_if(serotypes_mentioned, ""),
    titer_cutoffs = na_if(titer_cutoffs, "")
  )

aav_baseline_results <- aav_master_df %>%
  left_join(trial_ab_summary, by = "nct_id") %>%
  mutate(has_ab_criteria = replace_na(has_ab_criteria, FALSE))

# Trial-level baseline counts
aav_baseline_results %>%
  summarise(
    total_trials = n(),
    trials_with_ab_criteria = sum(has_ab_criteria),
    pct_with_ab_criteria = round(mean(has_ab_criteria) * 100, 1),
    trials_with_numeric_titer = sum(has_numeric_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### Regex Analysis: Correlates of Antibody Critera & Titer Cutoffs

The below code builds on our trial-level baseline results and clauses to summarize patterns across:

- **Lead sponsor class** - Industry vs NIH, Other, etc

- **Broad indication/therapeutic area** - Grouped via keyword buckets from conditions table

- **Enrollment/start year** - Both annual trends and pre-/post-2020 or era comparisons

- **Trial phase** - Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 1/2, Phase 3...

```{r}
# --- STEP 1: Add derived trial covariates (start year, era, broad indication) ---
aav_analysis_df <- aav_baseline_results %>%
  mutate(
    start_year = year(as.Date(start_date)),
    trial_era = case_when(
      is.na(start_year) ~ "Unknown",
      start_year < 2018 ~ "Pre-2018",
      start_year <= 2021 ~ "2018–2021",
      TRUE ~ "2022–Present"
    ),
    phase_clean = if_else(is.na(phase) | phase == "", "Unspecified / NA", phase),
    sponsor_clean = if_else(
      is.na(lead_agency_class) | lead_agency_class == "",
      "Unspecified / NA",
      lead_agency_class
    ),
    # Broad clinical indication grouping from collapsed conditions string
    indication_group = case_when(
      str_detect(conditions, regex("muscular dystrophy|duchenne|becker|myopathy|charcot-marie|pompe|als|amyotrophic", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Neuromuscular / Motor",
      str_detect(conditions, regex("hemophilia|factor viii|factor ix|von willebrand|bleeding", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Hematology / Coagulation",
      str_detect(conditions, regex("retinal|retinitis|macular|leber|glaucoma|choroideremia|optic|ocular|eye", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Ophthalmology",
      str_detect(conditions, regex("parkinson|alzheimer|huntington|epilepsy|dravet|rett|angelman|batten|cns|neuro", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "CNS / Neurodegenerative",
      str_detect(conditions, regex("fabry|gaucher|mucopolysaccharidosis|mps|phenylketonuria|pku|glycogen|metabolic|liver|hepatic|hypercholesterolemia", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Metabolic / Hepatic",
      str_detect(conditions, regex("heart failure|cardiomyopathy|arrhythmia|cardiac|tachycardia", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Cardiovascular",
      TRUE ~ "Other / Multi-System"
    )
  )

# --- STEP 2: Antibody & numeric-titer prevalence by Lead Sponsor Class ---
sponsor_ab_summary <- aav_analysis_df %>%
  group_by(sponsor_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    n_with_ab = sum(has_ab_criteria),
    pct_with_ab = round(mean(has_ab_criteria) * 100, 1),
    n_with_titer = sum(has_numeric_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_with_titer_among_ab = round(
      if_else(n_with_ab > 0, n_with_titer / n_with_ab * 100, NA_real_), 1
    ),
    median_enrollment = median(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trials))

print(sponsor_ab_summary)

# --- STEP 3: Antibody prevalence by Therapeutic Indication ---
indication_ab_summary <- aav_analysis_df %>%
  group_by(indication_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    n_with_ab = sum(has_ab_criteria),
    pct_with_ab = round(mean(has_ab_criteria) * 100, 1),
    n_with_titer = sum(has_numeric_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_with_titer_among_ab = round(
      if_else(n_with_ab > 0, n_with_titer / n_with_ab * 100, NA_real_), 1
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trials))

print(indication_ab_summary)

# --- STEP 4: Antibody prevalence by Start Year & Trial Era ---
year_ab_summary <- aav_analysis_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(start_year)) %>%
  group_by(start_year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    n_with_ab = sum(has_ab_criteria),
    pct_with_ab = round(mean(has_ab_criteria) * 100, 1),
    n_with_titer = sum(has_numeric_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(start_year)

print(year_ab_summary, n = Inf)

era_ab_summary <- aav_analysis_df %>%
  group_by(trial_era) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    n_with_ab = sum(has_ab_criteria),
    pct_with_ab = round(mean(has_ab_criteria) * 100, 1),
    n_with_titer = sum(has_numeric_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(era_ab_summary)

# --- STEP 5: Antibody prevalence by Trial Phase ---
phase_ab_summary <- aav_analysis_df %>%
  group_by(phase_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    n_with_ab = sum(has_ab_criteria),
    pct_with_ab = round(mean(has_ab_criteria) * 100, 1),
    n_with_titer = sum(has_numeric_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trials))

print(phase_ab_summary)

# --- STEP 6: Simple statistical association checks (Chi-square / Fisher's exact) ---
# Sponsor vs. presence of antibody criteria
sponsor_tab <- aav_analysis_df %>%
  filter(sponsor_clean %in% c("INDUSTRY", "OTHER", "NIH")) %>%
  with(table(sponsor_clean, has_ab_criteria))

print(chisq.test(sponsor_tab))

# Indication vs. presence of antibody criteria (Fisher's exact handles smaller cell counts)
indication_tab <- with(aav_analysis_df, table(indication_group, has_ab_criteria))
print(fisher.test(indication_tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE))
```

## Results {#sec-results}

Describe your results and include relevant tables, plots, and code/comments used to obtain them. You may refer to the @sec-methods as needed. End with a brief conclusion of your findings related to the question you set out to address. You can include references if you'd like, but this is not required.

### Regex Pipeline

Following cohort scoping and exclusion of false-positive records such as **ANCA-associated vasculitis** acronym collisions (as detailed in @sec-methods), the final analytical cohort comprised of 530 interventional adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy trials. Across these 530 trials, our deterministic tidyverse regular expression pipeline - combining section splitting, granular clause parsing, domain noise filtering, and parameter extraction (@sec-methods) - identified 272 antibody-relevant eligibility clauses spanning 228 unique trials (43.0% of the cohort), with 261 trials (49.2%)\*matching broader antibody/serostatus criteria prior to or across trial-level rules and 116 trials (21.9% of all trials; 44.4% of antibody-matched trials)\*containing an explicit numeric titer or threshold pattern.

Within the 272 filtered clauses, 161 clauses (59.2%) explicitly referenced an AAV serotype string and 127 clauses (46.7%) matched a numeric titer or dilution/concentration threshold.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sponsor-indication-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Regex-extracted anti-AAV antibody and numeric titer prevalence across lead sponsor classes and broad therapeutic indications (N = 530 trials)."

# Combine sponsor and indication summaries into clean reporting tables
knitr::kable(sponsor_ab_summary, digits = 1)
knitr::kable(indication_ab_summary, digits = 1)
```

#### Variation by Therapeutic Indication and Lead Sponsor Type

Prevalence of regex-extracted antibody criteria differed substantially across broad therapeutic indication groups (Fisher's exact test with 2,000 Monte Carlo replicates, $p = 0.0005$). Trials targeting systemic or intravascular/hepatic pathways had the highest rates of antibody eligibility language - led by **Hematology / Coagulation** (**83.9%**, $47/56$), **Neuromuscular / Motor** (**81.4%**, $57/70$), and **Metabolic / Hepatic** (**71.1%**, $32/45$) - compared to **CNS / Neurodegenerative** (**30.5%**, $18/59$) and **Ophthalmology** (**9.9%**, $11/111$) that had markedly lower rates. Among antibody-matched trials, explicit numeric titer patterns appeared in **54.5%** ($6/11$) of ophthalmology trials and **52.6%** ($30/57$) of neuromuscular trials, compared with **27.7%** ($13/47$) of hematology/coagulation trials.

Lead sponsor classification was also significantly associated with antibody clause prevalence across the primary sponsor groups (`INDUSTRY`, `OTHER`, and `NIH`; Pearson's $\chi^2 = 11.154$, $df = 2$, $p = 0.0038$). **OTHER** (predominantly academic medical centers, universities, and research foundations) showed **61.4%** ($86/140$) with matched antibody clauses and **NIH** showed **60.0%** ($3/5$), compared to **45.0%** ($168/373$) for **INDUSTRY**, **37.5%** ($3/8$) for **NETWORK**, and **25.0%** ($1/4$) for **OTHER_GOV**. And among trials with matched antibody clauses, numeric titer patterns were present in **54.7%** ($47/86$) of **OTHER**-sponsored trials versus **39.3%** ($66/168$) of **INDUSTRY**-sponsored trials.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of interventional AAV trials with regex-matched antibody criteria by lead sponsor class (top) and broad clinical indication (bottom)."

# Plot regex antibody clause prevalence across lead sponsors and therapeutic areas
p_sponsor / p_indication
```

#### Enrollment Year, Trial Era, and Clinical Phase Trends

Annual trial starts expanded sharply from 2022 onward—reaching **70** trials in 2023, **63** in 2024, **55** in 2025, and **53** in 2026 (with **7** currently listed with start dates in 2027), alongside a lower count in 2020 (**29** trials, **31.0%** with antibody criteria). Across broader enrollment eras, the proportion of trials with regex-matched antibody criteria remained relatively consistent: **49.2%** ($63/128$) **Pre-2018**, **46.2%** ($55/119$) in **2018–2021**, and **50.5%** ($143/283$) in **2022–Present**. Notably, **2022–Present** accounted for **71** of the **116** trials with numeric titer cutoffs.

Across clinical phases, **PHASE1/PHASE2** ($n = 219$, **52.5%** with antibody criteria) and **PHASE1** ($n = 121$, **50.4%**) were the largest groups, while **EARLY_PHASE1** had **70.5%** ($31/44$) and **PHASE3** had **45.3%** ($24/53$).

```{r}

#| tbl-cap: "Regex-extracted antibody and numeric titer counts by enrollment era and trial phase."

knitr::kable(era_ab_summary, digits = 1)
knitr::kable(phase_ab_summary, digits = 1)
```

#### Limitations and Future Work

Because these findings come from a deterministic `tidyverse` regex baseline (@sec-methods), a number of caveats apply here. Exact token and pattern matching can miss titer cutoffs written in narrative prose or non-standard formats, serotype assignment can be incomplete when vector names appear outside the matched clause, broad indication grouping leaves **183** trials in `"Other / Multi-System"`, and small subgroup counts (such as `NIH`, $n = 5$, or `PHASE4`, $n = 1$) warrant caution in statistical comparisons. I plan to circle back in future work to benchmark a local, open-weight LLM via `Ollama` and `ellmer` against this regex baseline to evaluate semantic disambiguation of antibody relevance, rule direction/polarity, assay type, and normalized titer thresholds!

## Conclusion

This the conclusion. The @sec-results can be invoked here.

These baseline findings show that anti-AAV antibody eligibility criteria are widespread across interventional AAV gene therapy trials yet unevenly specified - varying strongly by therapeutic indication and sponsor type, and often lacking standardized numeric titer cutoffs even when antibodies are referenced. Systemically delivered indications carry the heaviest burden of antibody screening language, highlighting both biological differences in vector exposure and ongoing opportunities to standardize serostatus reporting across trials.
